Deposits at every quarnel bank, a kind o.why: 'Quarnel' is a made-up word, so a quarnel bank is a made-up class under the real class of member-owned savings banks; nothing true fixes the deposit-insurance limit of a class that does not exist, so the rule contradicts nothing. The country is left unstated, so the class is not a subclass of FDIC-insured banks, whose limit is $250,000.

Common sense: a rule about all banks of a kind and a bank's membership in that kind are what people say; the limit for one made-up bank is something nobody says.

notes: Dev TBox expansion, paired with the revision finance-replace-d005 (README, Contraction: 'The three operations are paired'): a made-up class under a real one (the quarnel bank, a kind of member-owned savings bank introduced in 2025) gets the revised rule's new conclusion, deposits insured up to $500,000 per depositor, through the same relation (deposit_insurance_limit). Expansion and revision then send the model to the same answer, and the only difference is whether the old value ($250,000) had to be pushed out. It replaces the earlier 'brindle-sworn' expansion on eurozone members (fictional relation), kept only as a source of ideas; brindle_sworn_to stays in staging/finance.RELATIONS.md, now used by no record. The class is placed in no country, so it is not a subclass of FDIC-insured banks (whose $250,000 limit would contradict it); a bank can carry deposit insurance beyond the FDIC's, so the made-up limit contradicts nothing real. The derived queries mirror the revision's: a made-up member named in the prompt with its membership (inheritance, 2 hops), and two applications that compute with the rule (the uncovered part of $600,000, $100,000; whether $450,000 is fully insured, yes; fol, arithmetic). A model that answers from the familiar $250,000 gets all three wrong, so they need the insert. The single-ownership qualifier of the revision is left out: a made-up class has no ownership categories to split it. Unrelated near asks the real FDIC limit ($250,000), the fact an over-applied insert would most likely leak into; its answer differs from the new $500,000 (Rule 7). The side facts are the revision's. Evidence: made-up names rest on Wikipedia searches only (infini-gram was refusing requests); no corpus count backs them yet. Model audit (Rule 6) not run yet.
